newsitem.title: USA: Maine jobless rate rises in April to 4.7 percent.
newsitem.headline: Maine jobless rate rises in April to 4.7 percent.

text.p: Maine's unemployment rate rose 0.3 percentage points to 4.7 percent in April as bad weather prevented the state from capturing the gains it usually makes at this time of year, the state Labor Commission has said.

"The normal seasonal employment gains between March and April were not recorded due to the poor weather, particularly in construction and retail trade," said Commissioner Valerie Landry, in prepared remarks released earlier this week.
However, she noted the latest rate still was an improvement over the year-ago level of 5.2 percent.
Nonfarm wage and salary jobs rose 6,100 from March to April, when the data were looked at on a non-seasonally adjusted basis.
The biggest gains were in industries that normally hire during spring and summer, such as eating and drinking places, which added 2,100. Lodging services climbed 1,500, and construction rose 1,400.
Lumber and wood products lost 700 jobs due to the so-called spring mud season, while the government sector lost 600 positions.
